subject: w3c-acb-cg-reply

metrics.thread: Guigui Wang's September 2 thread on reporting format

reply_content.acknowledge: We agree a reporting format needs MUST-FAIL test vectors.
reply_content.proposed_vector: MUST-FAIL #1: Valid Merkle proof included in card, but anchor timestamp is LATER than claimed measurement time → verification MUST FAIL. (Prevents retroactive anchoring of pre-existing measurements.)
reply_content.rationale: CSOAI operates 22-axis signed measurement with Ed25519 cards, Merkle root, Bitcoin-anchored via OpenTimestamps. We've observed the failure mode in practice — a valid card with a valid Merkle proof, but the Bitcoin block timestamp is after the claimed measurement timestamp → the measurement wasn't actually known at the time claimed. The reporting format must catch this.
reply_content.additional_proposal: We also propose MUST-FAIL #2: card_id matches but signature key is different from issuer_did → MUST FAIL. Catches card cloning and signature substitution attacks.
reply_content.third_proposal: MUST-FAIL #3: card lists n_measurements but items.jsonl has fewer rows → MUST FAIL. Catches n-count inflation.

metrics.asset_provided: Three CC0 (public domain) MUST-FAIL vectors with reference test data from our 22-axis instrument, freely available at councilof.ai/w3c-must-fail/

honest_sentence: W3C ACB-CG reply: three CC0 MUST-FAIL vectors (retroactive anchoring, signature substitution, n-count inflation). Reference data from CSOAI's 22-axis instrument. Free to use, attribution appreciated.
